- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and prices are trending up, model often overcorrects; expect downward correction in next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 7–14 days.
- When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with recent 7-day moving average.
- If model forecast is consistently above true outcome by >3% over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence with observed trend.
- If sentiment history shows increasing negativity (e.g., 0.0 → 0.2 → 0.67), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% downward buffer to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, if model shows linear upward trend with no volatility, true outcome often exhibits sharp volatility or mean reversion; reduce forecast slope or add volatility buffer.
